title: Business Technology & AI Innovation
curriculumBasis: CHAMPUS groups practice into nine subjects for the PIB pilot. Your lecturer confirms the official syllabus and credit requirements.
practiceBasis: CHAMPUS proposes the outcomes, topics, practice, indicators and career examples. An authorized teacher can select an exercise and define the assessment.

courses.title: Web and Apps Development
courses.overview: Build a small browser application around one action. HTML gives each control a purpose. CSS arranges the controls. JavaScript responds when the user acts.
courses.outcome: Build a page that lets a user make a selection and see the result.
courses.practice: Sketch one screen. Add a labelled control and a result area. Use the page with a keyboard at phone and desktop widths. Save the result of each check.
courses.indicator: A reviewer can reach the control using the keyboard, change the selection and see the corresponding result at both widths.
courses.artifact: A runnable page and a short record of the four checks.

paths.developer: Build an issue queue. Let the user select an issue status and display matching tickets.
paths.photographer: Build a proof gallery. Let the client select a photo category and display the matching images.

courses.title: Database
courses.overview: A relational database stores related records in tables. A primary key identifies a record. A foreign key links that record to a related table.
courses.outcome: Model a one-to-many relationship and retrieve related records with a join.
courses.practice: Create two tables with primary keys. Add a foreign key to the child table. Insert sample records, run a join and try inserting a child with an unknown parent.
courses.indicator: The join returns the correct parent for each child. The database rejects a child whose parent is missing.
courses.artifact: A schema, sample inserts, a join query and the results of both checks.

paths.developer: Link releases to change requests and list the requests included in each release.
paths.photographer: Link shoots to image files and list the files delivered for each shoot.

courses.title: Human Behaviour
courses.overview: The setting can affect how a person acts. An observer can describe a pause, a question or a choice. The reason for that action requires further evidence.
courses.outcome: Separate an observed action from a possible explanation for it.
courses.practice: With permission, observe a volunteer doing a short task. Write down one action, two possible reasons and a neutral follow-up question. Remove identifying details.
courses.indicator: The note describes a visible action, considers a feature of the situation and keeps the volunteer's answer distinct from the observer's interpretation.
courses.artifact: An anonymous observation note with the follow-up question and response.

paths.developer: Observe a volunteer finding a setting in an app. Ask what they expected the menu label to mean.
paths.photographer: Observe a volunteer choosing a portrait from a contact sheet. Ask what details guided their choice.

courses.title: SEO and GEO
courses.overview: Search engine optimization helps people and search systems understand a page. Generative engine optimization concerns how content may appear in generated answers. Google describes common foundations for both on its own search service.
courses.outcome: Revise a page so a reader can find a supported answer to a specific search question.
courses.practice: Choose one question and inspect an existing page. Revise its title, heading and answer. Cite the source for each factual claim. Keep a copy of both versions.
courses.indicator: The revised page identifies the question, gives a direct answer and links to a source that supports the answer. Appearance in search results remains uncertain.
courses.artifact: The original and revised page with a short explanation of each change.

resource.title: Optimizing for generative AI features on Google Search

paths.developer: Revise a help page that answers a common setup question. Link to the versioned product documentation.
paths.photographer: Revise a portfolio FAQ about booking a session. Link to the published booking terms that support the answer.

courses.title: Digital Marketing
courses.overview: A campaign connects a defined audience, a message and an action. A useful measure specifies the event being counted, the denominator and the reporting period.
courses.outcome: Use a conversion measure to decide one change to a campaign.
courses.practice: Define a target action. For one channel and one period, record total visits and visits with the target action. Divide the second count by the first. Explain one limit of the result.
courses.indicator: Both counts cover the same channel and period. Each converted visit is counted once. The report identifies the denominator and leaves the rate undefined when there are no visits.
courses.artifact: A campaign brief and a worksheet showing the counts, calculation and proposed change.

resource.title: Metrics Used to Evaluate the Success of Online Marketing

paths.developer: Use visits to a product page and visits that lead to trial activation. Propose a change to the trial invitation.
paths.photographer: Use visits to a portfolio page and visits that lead to a booking enquiry. Propose a change to the enquiry invitation.

courses.title: Big Data
courses.overview: Distributed tools process data in partitions. A small practice dataset lets you check a transformation before applying it to a larger collection.
courses.outcome: Produce a repeatable grouped count and reconcile the result with the input.
courses.practice: Read two sample files with the same schema into a Spark DataFrame. Define a stable record ID. Remove duplicates by ID, count rows with missing categories and group the remaining records.
courses.indicator: Grouped totals plus the missing-category count equal the number of unique records. Running the same steps on the same input produces the same totals.
courses.artifact: A notebook, two small input files and a table that reconciles the counts.

paths.developer: Combine application event files. Use the event ID to remove duplicates and count events by event type.
paths.photographer: Combine image inventory exports. Use the asset ID to remove duplicates and count assets by usage licence.

courses.title: Business Model
courses.overview: A business model describes how a business serves a customer and covers its costs. The Business Model Canvas links customers, value, channels, resources and financial assumptions.
courses.outcome: Connect a customer need, a value proposition, a revenue source and a delivery cost in one model.
courses.practice: Draft a one-page canvas. Select one customer segment and follow its path from need to purchase and delivery. Flag one assumption and describe how you would test it.
courses.indicator: The model identifies who pays, what they receive and one cost of supplying it. A proposed test addresses a named assumption.
courses.artifact: An annotated canvas and one assumption test.

paths.developer: Model a scheduling service for small clinics. Connect the subscription price to the cost of hosting and support.
paths.photographer: Model a product photography service for food sellers. Connect the session fee to the cost of shooting and editing.

courses.title: Entrepreneurship
courses.overview: An opportunity begins with a problem that matters to a potential customer. Early research can reveal how people handle the problem today and whether an idea deserves another test.
courses.outcome: Use evidence from a customer conversation to decide which business assumption to test next.
courses.practice: Write one assumption about a customer's problem. With consent, ask a potential customer to describe a recent instance. Record the current workaround and one observation that challenges your idea.
courses.indicator: The record separates what the person reported from the student's interpretation. The proposed next test addresses uncertainty that the conversation exposed.
courses.artifact: An anonymous interview note, an assumption and a plan for the next test.

paths.developer: Ask a small business owner about the last time two customers booked the same slot. Use the current workaround to design a scheduling test.
paths.photographer: Ask a restaurant owner about the last time they needed a new menu image. Use their actual process to design a service trial.

courses.title: English for Business
courses.overview: A professional email makes an arrangement the reader can confirm. A clear message identifies the purpose, date, time zone and requested response.
courses.outcome: Write a concise English email that enables a business contact to confirm an arrangement.
courses.practice: Draft a subject line and a short message. Propose a date and time with a time zone. State what each participant needs to prepare. Ask the recipient to confirm or suggest an alternative.
courses.indicator: A reader can identify the purpose, proposed time, preparation and next action without asking for missing details.
courses.artifact: A draft email and a short peer check of the four details.

paths.developer: Email a client to arrange a product walkthrough. Name the version and ask them to bring one task they want to test.
paths.photographer: Email a client to arrange a pre-shoot meeting. Name the location and ask them to bring a brief and a shot list.
